prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

Method performed by a network node for reducing interference in neighboring cells. The network node operates in a communication network, which is adapted to wirelessly serve a UE via a serving Radio Access, RA, node. The network node obtains a determination of at least one of Reference Signal Received Power, RSRP, and Reference Signal Received Quality, RSRQ, from the serving RA node as received by the UE and a determination of at least one of RSRP and RSRQ from a neighboring RA node as received by the UE, when the UE is connected to the serving RA node. The network node further decides to reduce a transmit power of the serving RA node serving the connected UE, when the determined RSRP and/or RSRQ of the serving RA node is higher than the RSRP and/or RSRQ of the neighboring RA node, in order to reduce the interference in neighboring cells caused by the serving RA node.

outputs.L1: A method performed by a network node for reducing interference in neighboring cells. The network node operates in a communication network configured to wirelessly serve a user equipment (UE) via a serving Radio Access (RA) node. While the UE is connected to the serving RA node, the network node obtains a determination of at least one of Reference Signal Received Power (RSRP) and Reference Signal Received Quality (RSRQ) from the serving RA node, as received by the UE, and a determination of at least one of RSRP and RSRQ from a neighboring RA node, as received by the UE. The network node further decides to reduce the transmit power of the serving RA node serving the connected UE when the determined RSRP and/or RSRQ of the serving RA node is higher than the RSRP and/or RSRQ of the neighboring RA node, thereby reducing interference in neighboring cells caused by the serving RA node.
outputs.L2: A network node in a wireless communication system performs a procedure to limit interference affecting adjacent cells. The system provides wireless service to a user equipment (UE) through a serving Radio Access (RA) node. While the UE is connected to the serving RA node, the network node obtains measured values for Reference Signal Received Power (RSRP), Reference Signal Received Quality (RSRQ), or both, for signals received by the UE from the serving RA node. It also obtains corresponding RSRP, RSRQ, or both measurements for signals received by the UE from a neighboring RA node. If the serving RA node’s measured RSRP and/or RSRQ exceeds that of the neighboring RA node, the network node determines that the serving RA node’s transmit power should be lowered, thereby reducing interference caused by the serving RA node in neighboring cells.

A network node is configured to reduce interference in neighboring cells of a wireless communication network. The network serves a user equipment (UE) through a serving Radio Access (RA) node. To assess potential interference, the network node obtains Reference Signal Received Power (RSRP) and/or Reference Signal Received Quality (RSRQ) measurements for both the serving RA node and a neighboring RA node, as measured by the connected UE.

The network node compares the RSRP and/or RSRQ measurements associated with the serving RA node with the corresponding measurements associated with the neighboring RA node. If the comparison indicates that the serving RA node’s RSRP and/or RSRQ is higher than that of the neighboring RA node, the network node reduces its transmit power. This power reduction helps limit interference caused in neighboring cells while maintaining communication with the connected UE.
outputs.L4:
A network node may control downlink transmission power to reduce inter-cell interference based on radio measurements reported by one or more user equipments (UEs). Each UE measures reference signals transmitted by its serving radio access node and by one or more neighboring radio access nodes. The measurements may include reference signal received power (RSRP), reference signal received quality (RSRQ), or both. The UE reports the measurements to the serving node or to another network entity responsible for coordinating radio resources and transmission power.

The network node compares the measurement associated with the serving radio access node with the corresponding measurement associated with a neighboring node. For example, the node may determine a difference between the serving-cell RSRP and the neighboring-cell RSRP, a difference between the serving-cell RSRQ and the neighboring-cell RSRQ, or a combined metric based on both measurements. If the serving-cell signal exceeds the neighboring-cell signal by a specified threshold, the network may infer that the UE has sufficient serving-cell coverage and that the serving node can reduce its transmission power without materially degrading the UE’s connection.

In response, the network lowers the serving node’s transmit power. The reduction may apply to the entire cell, a selected carrier, bandwidth part, beam, antenna port, physical channel, reference signal, time interval, frequency resource, or group of resource blocks. The amount of the reduction may be fixed or may depend on the measured difference, the UE’s service requirements, the current traffic load, or an interference target. A larger measurement margin may permit a larger power reduction, whereas a smaller margin may result in a smaller reduction or no change.

Reducing the serving node’s transmit power decreases the energy received by UEs in neighboring cells and therefore mitigates inter-cell interference. The resulting interference reduction can improve signal quality, reliability, and resource utilization in those cells. At the same time, the serving node may continue monitoring UE measurement reports, link quality, retransmission rates, throughput, and other performance indicators to ensure that the reduced power remains adequate.

The power-control decision may include thresholds, hysteresis, filtering, or timers to avoid frequent changes caused by short-term fading or measurement fluctuations. If subsequent reports indicate that the serving-cell RSRP or RSRQ has fallen relative to a neighboring cell, or that serving-cell performance no longer satisfies a required criterion, the network may stop the reduction or increase the transmit power. In this manner, transmission power is adapted dynamically to preserve serving-cell coverage while limiting unnecessary interference to neighboring cells.

### The Radio Method

The radio was more than an old machine on the kitchen shelf; it was a method of reaching beyond the silence. Every evening, Mara turned the dial slowly, searching through static for distant voices, music, and news from places she had never seen.

counterfactuals.output:
1. **A method for reducing inter-cell interference, the method comprising:**  
   
   receiving, by a serving radio access node from a user equipment served by the serving radio access node, a measurement report comprising:  
   a first measurement associated with a reference signal transmitted by the serving radio access node; and  
   a second measurement associated with a reference signal transmitted by a neighboring radio access node,  
   wherein the first measurement and the second measurement each comprise at least one of a reference signal received power (RSRP) measurement or a reference signal received quality (RSRQ) measurement;  
   
   comparing the first measurement with the second measurement;  
   
   determining, based on the comparing, that a power-reduction criterion is satisfied, the power-reduction criterion indicating that coverage of the serving radio access node overlaps coverage of the neighboring radio access node; and  
   
   responsive to determining that the power-reduction criterion is satisfied, reducing a transmit power used by the serving radio access node for at least one downlink transmission, thereby reducing interference caused by the serving radio access node in the coverage of the neighboring radio access node.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe a network-node method that uses signal-strength or signal-quality measurements from a connected UE to decide whether to lower the transmit power of its serving base station.
counterfactuals.output:
A network node can control serving-cell transmit power as follows:

1. **Obtain measurements:** Receive measurement reports from a UE connected to a serving base station. The reports include serving-cell signal strength or quality, such as RSRP, RSSI, RSRQ, or SINR, and optionally corresponding neighbor-cell measurements.

2. **Evaluate radio conditions:** Compare the serving-cell measurement with one or more configured thresholds. The node may also verify that:
   - the serving signal remains above a minimum coverage or quality threshold;
   - the UE has sufficient link margin;
   - neighboring-cell interference is excessive or the serving signal is stronger than necessary; and
   - the condition persists for a specified time or number of reports.

3. **Decide on power reduction:** If the measurements indicate that the UE can maintain an acceptable connection at a lower serving-cell power, determine a reduced transmit-power level or a power-reduction step.

4. **Apply the reduction:** Send a control instruction to the serving base station, or internally configure its transmitter, to lower the relevant downlink transmit power.

5. **Monitor and adjust:** Continue receiving UE reports. Stop or reverse the reduction if signal strength or quality falls below a safety threshold, handover risk increases, or service performance degrades.

Hysteresis, filtering, minimum/maximum power limits, and time-to-trigger criteria can be used to prevent repeated power oscillations.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a technical abstract about interference mitigation in neighboring cellular-network cells using comparisons of serving-cell and neighboring-cell RSRP/RSRQ.
counterfactuals.output: **Abstract—** Inter-cell interference at cellular network boundaries can significantly degrade user throughput, reliability, and spectral efficiency. This work presents an interference-mitigation framework based on joint comparison of Reference Signal Received Power (RSRP) and Reference Signal Received Quality (RSRQ) measurements from the serving cell and neighboring cells. The proposed method uses RSRP differences to estimate relative cell dominance and RSRQ differences to distinguish coverage limitations from interference-dominated conditions. User equipment is classified as cell-center, cell-edge, or interference-limited according to configurable measurement thresholds and time-to-trigger filtering. For interference-limited users, the serving cell initiates coordinated mitigation actions, including handover, transmit-power adjustment, resource-block coordination, beam adaptation, or enhanced inter-cell interference coordination. Hysteresis and temporal averaging are applied to reduce measurement noise, ping-pong handovers, and unnecessary coordination signaling. The framework can be implemented using standard measurement reports and extended with load, mobility, and channel-quality information. System-level evaluation indicates that combining serving- and neighboring-cell RSRP/RSRQ provides more reliable interference detection than power-only methods, improving cell-edge link quality and resource allocation while preserving overall network capacity.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3
